channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: 2 teenagers arrested for alleged plot targeting California high school, police say
item.description: Two 15-year-old high school students were arrested on suspicion of preparing to carry out a school shooting at Corona High School in California, police said.

item.title: Detained American Stephen Hubbard released by Russia as Witkoff meets Putin
item.description: President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff landed in the Russian city of St. Petersburg on Wednesday morning, a Kremlin aide confirmed.

item.title: US envoy Steve Witkoff thanks Vladimir Putin for diesel deal at Ukraine talks in Russia
item.description: US envoy Steve Witkoff is in Saint Petersburg, holding talks with Russian president Vladimir Putin. The face to face meeting comes after he met with Ukraine's president and other European leaders in Oslo. Witkoff is due to return to the Norwegian capital after his visit to Russia. Washington seeks to breathe new life into US-led efforts to end the war. Details and analysis by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor, Kethevane Gorjestani.

item.title: Ukraine talks: US envoy meets Vladimir Putin in Russia
item.description: US envoy Steve Witkoff held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday about Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, as US President Donald Trump pushes Kyiv to make a deal that stops the fighting. The day before, the American official had met with Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo, Norway. Details by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Philip Turle.

item.title: Egypt mulls joining Saudi Arabia in war against Houthis
item.description: Egypt may be about to join the war against Houthis. Saudi Arabia has come under sustained attack from the Iran-backed group in recent weeks after a collapse of a truce in Yemen in September. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman visited Egypt mid-September to request potential military support from the country – a demand put before parliament by the Egyptian president on Saturday. Story by Camille Corcoran.

item.title: WATCH: $1 million heist nets rare Pokémon cards
item.description: Nearly $1 million in rare trading cards were stolen from a FedEx truck parked near a Southern California business that authenticates and grades the collectible items, according to police.

item.title: Musk talks up potential merger of SpaceX and Tesla
item.description: As SpaceX reports blockbuster quarterly earnings, CEO Elon Musk floats the possibility of merging the rocketry and AI firm with his electric car company Tesla. Also in this edition: OpenAI reveals more agent misbehaviour as market turmoil hits data centre companies, and France's political crisis exacerbates its bond market rout.

item.title: French Prime Minister vows 'massive' police deployment for new demonstrations
item.description: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has vowed a "massive" police deployment for the fresh demonstrations called for Saturday by the "Yellow Vest" movement. Facing angry lawmakers in parliament, Lecornu acknowledged that the security response had fallen short and promised a stronger approach ahead of this new wave of protests.

item.title: Garda investigation launched as two bodies found in Ireland
item.description: A Garda investigation has been launched after two bodies were discovered in Ireland.

item.title: REPLAY: French president addresses fuel supplies during Gulf tour
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Tuesday he had secured the delivery of an additional 200,000 tonnes of diesel per month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. He is currently in Doha as part of a tour of the Gulf. "We are reducing our dependency" he said whilst speaking to the press on October 21.

item.title: WATCH: Controversy brews over home of Winnie the Pooh
item.description: ABC News' Danny New examines a controversy about where the stuffed bear that inspired Winnie the Pooh should reside: in England or the New York Public Library?

item.title: Amy Acton campaign slams Ramaswamy over controversial ad featuring estranged mother
item.description: Ohio Gubernatorial Candidate Amy Acton’s campaign alleged her opponent's campaign is using her estranged mother in a controversial political ad against her.

item.title: Italy deploys troops into Milan in response to recent riots
item.description: Italy approved troop deployment after intense riots in Milan. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni toughened security laws after clashes between youths and the police, following a weekend of unrest in several Italian cities. FRANCE 24's correspondent Seema Gupta reports from the ground.

item.title: Ukraine talks: What progress after US envoy met with Zelensky?
item.description: US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff is headed to Russia today to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin for peace talks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, on his end, met with the US official in Norway Tuesday. What progress has been made in Oslo? Ophélie Jacobson explains.

item.title: Amber warning issued ahead of Storm Austen
item.description: An amber wind warning has been issued for the South West of England on Friday, with gusts of up to 80mph expected.

item.title: Women lead the charge for Saudi contemporary art
item.description: Saudi artists Reem Ali and Bashaer Hawsawi are showing installations that explore the domestic space, feminine spheres and the emotionally charged meaning of the table, in a group show presented by the Villa Hegra as part of the Asia Now art fair in Paris.

item.title: Actor Noel Clarke pleads not guilty to six sexual offences
item.description: Actor Noel Clarke has pleaded not guilty to six sexual offences.

item.title: French PM vows stronger security as country prepares for more protests
item.description: French prime minister Sebastien Lecornu and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez both faced tough questions from members of parliament over the handling of last weekend's violence. Lecornu has promised a massive deployment of police for future protests, while Nunez said the military will be used to back up the security forces. Details by FRANCE 24’s Ellen Gainsford live from the prime minister's office.

item.title: Expecting a baby? 5 tips to help you prepare for pregnancy costs
item.description: The cost of having a baby is difficult to predict. The amount families pay varies widely. Here are five tips to help you prepare for the often unexpected costs of pregnancy and giving birth.

item.title: Italy deploys army and approves tougher anti-riot laws after violence
item.description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Tuesday announced the deployment of 500 troops to Milan to assist police following clashes in the city. Meloni said a cabinet meeting also approved measures to make the detention of minors easier and to impose fines on their parents for any damage. Story by Morgan Ayre.

item.title: At least 153 people killed in drone strike on disputed Sudan-South Sudan region
item.description: A drone strike on a fuel depot in a disputed region on the Sudan-South Sudan border has killed at least 153 people.

item.title: Champions League: Paris defeat Barcelona but lose three major players to injuries
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain beat FC Barcelona (4-2) and have moved to the top of the Champions League table. However, Ousmane Dembélé, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia were all forced off through injury.

item.title: Man arrested in Pakistan over $126m counterfeit postage scheme
item.description: A man has been arrested in Pakistan and accused of running a counterfeit postage operation costing the US Postal Service $126m (£94m).

item.title: Justice Kagan warns Supreme Court rulings fueling polarization, undermining democracy
item.description: Justice Elena Kagan says decisions by her conservative Supreme Court colleagues have increased political polarization and weakened democracy in the U.S. She spoke Tuesday, two weeks before the midterm elections, criticizing rulings that weakened the Vo...

item.title: Boy, 16, found guilty of attempted murder after stabbing girl at school
item.description: A 16-year-old boy has been found guilty of attempted murder after stabbing a 15-year-old girl in the back at school.

item.title: LeBron James talks smack with Knicks fans in victorious 76ers debut
item.description: The Sixers got a first look at the potent lineup they put together this summer in hopes of winning their first title since 1983.

item.title: FAA clears the way for airlines to put Boeing's long-delayed 737 Max 10 into service
item.description: Nearly a decade after Boeing unveiled its largest 737 Max jet, the company has cleared a major hurdle in its effort to bring the plane to airlines.

item.title: Zelenskyy says early warning system for Russian missile attacks resumes
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the change happened after talks with his American counterparts, including a phone call with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

item.title: France announces nightly curfews 'for as long as necessary' in Paris and other cities
item.description: Fresh curfews were being imposed across the city centers of Paris and Lyon on Tuesday after the first quiet night since France's most destructive rioting in years.

item.title: Exceeding key climate target is now 'imminent and unavoidable'
item.description: Exceeding a key global climate target is now "imminent and unavoidable", United Nations (UN) scientists have warned.

item.title: Russia releases US citizen accused of fighting for Ukraine, Putin says during Witkoff meeting
item.description: US special envoy Steve Witkoff is meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg Wednesday after talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo. Putin said during the meeting that Russia had released US citizen Stephen Hubbard, who has been imprisoned for years in Russia after being charged of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine.

item.title: Rogers says inroads with Black and Jewish voters will help him beat El-Sayed
item.description: He broke with Trump on some tariffs and said he’s “worried” about the economy.

item.title: Boeing's 737 Max 10 finally wins FAA approval after years of delays
item.description: Boeing's largest 737 Max jet has cleared a major regulatory hurdle, with US aviation authorities approving the Max 10 for passenger service on Tuesday after nearly a decade of delays. The certification marks a boost for the planemaker's recovery, with deliveries expected to begin in 2027.

item.title: Live: Those who want to cause chaos will not be allowed to, Macron says ahead of Saturday protests
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said during a visit to Qatar Wednesday that those seeking to "cause chaos" at the nationwide demonstrations planned for Saturday will be prevented from doing so. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will meet with trade union organisations on Wednesday to discuss protest security and responses to the high school students who set off the initial wave of demonstrations. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Uganda reacts angrily as Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case
item.description: Nigeria has recorded its first case of Ebola during the current outbreak, the country's health ministry has said - as the virus continues to spread internationally.

item.title: WATCH: Great white shark leaps out of ocean off California's Marina Beach
item.description: A great white shark surprised visitors off Marina Beach, California, when it leapt out of the ocean as a beachgoer was taking a video.

item.title: Italy announces new security measures after Milan riots, deploying 500 soldiers
item.description: Italy announced tougher security measures on Tuesday after weekend riots in Milan left more than 100 police officers injured and shops looted. The government will deploy 500 additional soldiers, impose harsher penalties for violent protesters and hold parents financially responsible for damage caused by minors.

item.title: Nigeria records first Ebola case as outbreak spreads across Africa
item.description: Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case in Africa's latest outbreak, while Kenya reported its ninth infection, raising fears of further spread across the continent. Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya warned of an “extremely serious threat” and urged the international community to send funding, medical supplies and health workers.

item.title: AI on the ballot? Voters in US midterms revolt against data centres
item.description: Two weeks out from the US midterm elections, there's bipartisan pushback against data centres that suck the water and power out of communities. Just two years ago, ChatGPT was still a brand-new thing, and AI was admired with awe by most voters. Like in 2024, the hot-button issue in swing constituencies remains inflation, or "the price of eggs". But anxiety over the end of the month is now coupled with anxiety over the end of the world.

item.title: WATCH: Trump says what Russia is doing to Ukraine is 'fine'
item.description: Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Bill Taylor reacts to the latest comments from President Donald Trump on Russia as questions grow over America's support of Ukraine.

item.title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case
item.description: In tonight's programme: Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case in the midst of an outbreak that began in DR Congo in mid-May. Also, a former top South African police officer facing sexual grooming and rape charges is denied bail. Finally, São Tomé and Príncipe's rich volcanic soils produce vanilla pods with an entrancing taste unlike those grown anywhere else.

item.title: Egypt involvement in Yemen 'may actually weaken Cairo's regional role', expert says
item.description: Egypt's parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week, state media reported, after an emergency session ended without a decision a day earlier. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Dr May Darwich, Associate Professor in International Relations of the Middle East at the University of Birmingham. She explains that "this kind of military operation does not really have any objectives or exit strategy so at the moment this might actually weaken Egypt's regional role".

item.title: PSG end Barcelona's winning run as Liverpool fight back against Villarreal
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain came from behind to beat Barcelona 4-2 in a Champions League thriller on Tuesday, handing the Catalans their first defeat of the season. Liverpool staged a dramatic comeback to edge Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield, while Manchester City cruised to a 5-1 victory over AEK Athens.

item.title: Brazil’s presidential candidates push to have one another disqualified ahead of run-off
item.description: Both candidates in Brazil's presidential election called for their rival's disqualification Tuesday over allegations of social media malfeasance, according to court filings. Left-wing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s campaign said they will request the annulment of right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro's candidacy over alleged election interference by tech giant Meta, while Bolsonaro's team is accusing Lula of "abuse of power" in the mass sharing of government postings on WhatsApp.

item.title: NJ food importer files lawsuit challenging Trump's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods
item.description: A New Jersey food importer filed a lawsuit Tuesday challenging President Donald Trump’s power to invoke a Depression-era law to levy a 50% tariff on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods

item.title: WATCH: DHS: Ukrainians Retain Protection Pending TPS Decision
item.description: While the temporary protected status for thousands of Ukrainians has expired, the DHS says they can remain for now. Ukrainian student Mariia Hlyten discusses her unclear future in the U.S.

item.description: A 65-year-old woman was killed in a shark attack at a popular beach on South Africa's southeastern coast, local authorities said.

item.description: President Donald Trump took the stage in Kansas on Monday night to campaign for Sen. Roger Marshall, a one-term incumbent facing a close race against Adam Hamilton.

item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.description: Some older siblings have been left to care for their younger family members following the deportation of their parents, advocacy groups say.

item.description: Jason Chen of The New York Times' Wirecutter shares the technological products that are most loved by readers.

item.description: Open enrollment for Medicare, the nationwide federal health insurance program primarily for those aged 65 and older, began last week and there are some changes.

item.description: ABC News' Ian Pannell reports on the state of the agency, which says it's been providing food to around 1.6 million people every month since last year's ceasefire announcement.

item.description: A man has been arrested after a fire at the town hall of Limoges, according to French media.

item.description: Four soldiers from El Salvador are unaccounted for after being attacked by heavily-armed gangs in Haiti.

item.title: WATCH: Study shows Gulf oil spill's lasting damage
item.description: More than 16 years after the BP oil spill off the Gulf Coast, new research reveals lasting damage to marine life.

item.title: Albanians set fire to government buildings and clash with riot police in latest protests
item.description: Demonstrators in Albania have set fire to government buildings and banks, smashed shop windows during the latest clashes with police as they demand the prime minister's resignation.

item.title: Rep. Adam Smith joins lawmakers who received letter with 'suspicious substance'
item.description: Washington State Democratic Congressman Adam Smith received a “suspicious letter containing a powdery substance” on Monday.

item.description: President Donald Trump took his midterm pitch to Kansas Monday night, announcing a new fuel relief program for farmers facing record-high diesel prices.

item.title: Australian MP hit by car has both legs amputated as suspect appears in court
item.description: An Australian MP hit by a car has had both of her legs amputated, her husband has said.

item.title: Trump's approval rating hits new record low as US midterms loom
item.description: Donald Trump's approval rating has fallen to a record low - indicating that next month's midterm elections could be punishing for the Republicans.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir reports on the beloved barn owls that have made Manhattan home
item.description: An expert says it’s the first documented instance of barn owls nesting in Manhattan in modern history.

item.title: WATCH: Teen on how he turned 3D printing idea into a profitable business
item.description: Just three months after graduating high school, Mike Satterlee began using his 3D printer to make hard-shell insulated drink koozies he calls "can coolers."

item.description: A landmark report is set to detail the vast scale of antisemitism in English schools and colleges, Sky News can reveal.

item.description: Lawmakers on Capitol Hill are considering bills to keep cash an option in commerce.

item.description: ABC News' Danny New interviews a blind college student in Virginia who's traveling with her guide dog Beasley as she continues her education in Scotland.
